question.prompt: Triangle \(BAD\) is right-angled at \(B.\) On \(AD\) there is a point \(C\) for which \(AC=CD\) and \(AB=BC.\) The magnitude of angle \(DAB,\) in degrees, is:

solutions.explanation:
The condition \(AC=CD\) says that \(C\) is the midpoint of \(AD\). Because \(\triangle BAD\) is right-angled at \(B\), the side \(AD\) is its hypotenuse.

The midpoint of a right triangle's hypotenuse is equally distant from all three vertices. Therefore
\[
 AC=BC=CD.
\]
The given equality \(AB=BC\) now shows that \(AB=BC=CA\), so \(\triangle ABC\) is equilateral and \(\angle CAB=60^\circ\).

Since \(C\) lies on segment \(AD\), the rays \(AC\) and \(AD\) coincide. Hence \(\angle DAB=\angle CAB=60^\circ\), choice B.
solutions.title: Recognize an equilateral triangle
